# DIARRHEA WITH ESCHERICHIA COLI

## Enteroaggretive E. coli (EAEC), Enteropathogenic E. coli (EPEC), and

## Enterotoxigenic E. coli (ETEC)

Antibiotic therapy is not required for mild to moderate disease caused by these organisms because diarrhea often resolves on its own. Do not use antimotility agents in patients with bloody stool. Antimicrobial treatment in patients with AIDS Treatment is complex, consult Infectious Diseases
Primary treatment: Hydration and electrolyte replacement Antimicrobial treatment of severe diarrhea

## Enterohemorrhagic E. coli (EHEC) and Shiga Toxin-producing E. coli (STEC)

EHEC and STEC disease often presents as bloody diarrhea.
Treatment includes supportive measures such as volume repletion and administering appropriate nutrition. Do not use antimotility or antimicrobial agents as they can increase shiga-toxin release and increase the risk of hemolytic uremia syndrome (HUS).

## Enteroinvasive E. coli (EIEC)

EIEC disease typically presents as watery diarrhea, sometimes progressing to bloody diarrhea. Refer to Shigella/Enteroinvasive E. coli treatment recommendations.
